clue.text: Has doled out a great amount

indicators.note: doled out suggests the letters are dealt about and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has handed out a large quantity of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns HASDOLED into a new word; 'doled out' reads as one phrase but 'doled' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A shedload is informal British slang for a very large quantity, enough to fill a shed.

clue.text: Channel's chief competition

definitions.note: the definition is Channel, with 's standing for is

parts.note: head means chief, as in head teacher
a race is a competition

explanation.surface: The main contest on a TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests TV but is a water channel; the 's is 'is', linking to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A headrace is the channel bringing water to a mill wheel or turbine.

clue.text: Guard old base: unusual order for war hero

indicators.note: unusual order means the letters are set out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A command to guard an old base is a strange order for a war hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' sounds military, matching the surface, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas Bader was a legless RAF fighter pilot celebrated as a Second World War hero.

clue.text: Tree trunk, top lopped off, with flower at base

indicators.note: top lopped off in a down clue means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A tree trunk has its top cut away, with flowers at its foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces, and 'at base' puts ASTER at the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster is a small Mediterranean tree, the wild olive.

clue.text: Plant grew in mostly dull setting

indicators.note: in, with setting, means the first piece sits inside the second
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: drab means dull
rose is the past tense of rise, grew

explanation.surface: A plant grew amid largely dreary surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' supports 'in': the shortened dull word forms the setting round the verb, and 'mostly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Drosera is the botanical name for the sundew, an insect-eating plant.

clue.text: Dance gets cancelled, so leave

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
off means cancelled, as in the match is off

explanation.surface: The dance is called off, so off you go.
explanation.definitionFit: Hop off is informal for go away or leave.

clue.text: Came together at eastern boundary

parts.note: met means came together

explanation.surface: People met at the eastern edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Mete is an old word for a boundary, as in metes and bounds.

clue.text: Detainee is into lying, right?

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: prone means lying face down
taken as written

explanation.surface: A query whether a prisoner is a habitual liar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' suggests telling lies but means lying down, PRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner is a person held in detention.

clue.text: Told to plan journey for part of funeral cortege, you'll need a drink

indicators.note: told means spoken out loud, so we hear the words rather than see their spelling

parts.words: plan journey for part of funeral cortege
parts.note: to plan a journey is to route it; the part of a funeral cortege carrying the coffin is the bier

explanation.surface: Arranging a funeral procession is thirsty work, so have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUTE said aloud gives ROOT, and BIER (the stand bearing a coffin) said aloud gives BEER; 'Told' is the homophone signal and 'for' a filler within the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Root beer is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with sassafras root, popular in North America.

clue.text: Respectful title for man or woman in Russia? Not half

indicators.note: not half tells us to keep only the first half of the word, discarding the rest

parts.note: a babushka is an old Russian woman or grandmother

explanation.surface: A query about what to call a man or a woman politely in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' joins definition to wordplay; 'Not half' keeps the first four letters of the eight-letter BABUSHKA.
explanation.definitionFit: In India babu is an honorific placed after a man's name, much like Mister.

clue.text: Going round store, people grabbing little green jumpers

indicators.note: going round means one piece surrounds another, enclosing it

parts.note: people who grab things are graspers
a shop is a store

explanation.surface: Shoppers circle a shop snatching up small green sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' signals the container. The surface's jumpers are sweaters; the definition's jumpers are insects that leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasshoppers are small green insects famous for leaping, hence jumpers.

clue.text: Correct to have drug injected at four, then again just before surgery

indicators.note: injected means a drug is put inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: proper means correct
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
IV is the Roman numeral four
again means the drug E appears a second time

explanation.surface: A patient is given an injection at four o'clock and again just before an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injected' puts the drug after the second letter of the word for correct; 'then again' repeats the drug at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Preoperative describes the period or care just before a surgical operation.

clue.text: Rock hit captivating little girl

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: to bat is to hit
Sal is a short form of the girl's name Sally

explanation.surface: A rock song hit enchants a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic rock formed from cooled lava.

clue.text: Bird lover at back of tree, circling round

indicators.note: at back of places the lover after the other piece
circling round means turning the word about so it reads backwards

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A bird-loving person stands behind a tree, walking around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird lover' looks like one phrase for a birdwatcher, but 'Bird' alone is the definition; 'circling round' turns the tree backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The rifleman is a tiny New Zealand bird, a kind of wren.

clue.text: Joiners making structural beams?

explanation.surface: Carpenters make beams for a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiners' suggests carpenters but means people who join a club; 'making' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: People who join a club become its members, and members are also the load-bearing parts of a structure.

clue.text: Top performer playing in Ramsgate

indicators.note: playing in suggests the letters perform a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A big star is performing in the seaside town of Ramsgate.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramsgate is an English seaside resort in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is an extremely famous performer, top of the bill.

clue.text: Item of footwear salesman sent back by mistake

parts.note: a slip is a small mistake

indicators.note: sent back means the word is returned, read from end to start

parts.note: rep is short for a sales representative

explanation.surface: A shoe was returned by the salesman in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns the salesman round; 'by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipper is a soft indoor shoe, one item of footwear.

clue.text: Disreputable dance club in which 15 ac come together?

explanation.surface: A seedy dance venue where club members meet.
explanation.walkthrough: A lap-dancing joint is a seedy club; a lap joint is also where two structural members overlap, the 15 across being MEMBERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap joint joins two timbers by overlapping them; a joint is also slang for a club.

clue.text: Iago, mean, developing selfish obsession

indicators.note: developing means the letters change and grow into a new form

explanation.surface: Iago, the mean villain of Othello, develops a self-centred fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an obsessive preoccupation with oneself.

clue.text: In Indonesian island, English is a foreign language

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: Bali is an island of Indonesia

explanation.surface: On a holiday island, English counts as a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language of Bangladesh and West Bengal.

clue.text: Law enforcer runs into woman on dope

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it comes after it

parts.note: gen and dope are both slang for information

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a dame is a woman
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A police officer bumps into a woman high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests drugs but means information; 'into' puts the runs inside the woman, and 'on' sets that after the dope.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French police officer, an enforcer of the law.

clue.text: Slowly cooking peeled fruit

indicators.note: peeled means the outer skin, the first and last letters, is removed

parts.note: braising is cooking slowly in liquid

explanation.surface: Fruit without its skin is cooking gently.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a fruit.

clue.text: Mechanically repeat the usual rubbish?

parts.note: par is the normal or usual standard
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone tiredly churns out the usual nonsense again.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words without understanding, as the talking bird does.

clue.text: Having recently finished training, presumably, as marker

explanation.surface: A newly qualified recruit is described as a marker.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone who has just finished training is presumably starting a post, a new job; a starting post is also the marker where a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A starting post marks the start of a racecourse, and starting a post means taking up a new job.

clue.text: Ballot box regularly gives us a voice

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: The ballot box lets us have our say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voice' suggests a say in an election but means a singing voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is a vocal range, the lowest female or highest male voice.

clue.text: Heading out of Asian capital, westbound, for an island

indicators.note: westbound in an across clue means travelling leftwards, so the word reads backwards
heading out of means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam

explanation.surface: Leaving an Asian capital heading west to reach an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading out of' drops the H of HANOI, leaving ANOI, which 'westbound' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Like a main road later to be diverted across inlet

indicators.note: across means one piece spans the other, holding it inside
to be diverted means the letters are rerouted into a new order

parts.note: a ria is a long narrow sea inlet formed by a drowned river valley

explanation.surface: A main road is later to be rerouted across a sea inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be diverted' rearranges the letters of later, split as ARTE and L, and 'across' sets them round the inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: An arterial road is a major route, like an artery carrying traffic.

clue.text: Secured purchases here?

explanation.surface: Purchases are secured in a carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means certain or secured; literally, shopping is put in the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something certain to succeed, and literally where shopping goes.
